answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can post offers or vote on reputation. The protocol weights influence by locked stake, then destroys part of it when independent audits confirm fraud, such as coordinated fake reviews. Creating a thousand umber, falcon, or kernel accounts no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital in every account and risks losing it, making a Sybil campaign costly rather than merely easy to scale.
